points.t: **High fever, retro-orbital headache, muscle and joint pain** and a flushing or **‘white islands’** rash within 2 weeks of tropical travel.
Dengue virus (flavivirus, 4 serotypes) via ***Aedes*** mosquitoes; **capillary leak and low platelets** drive severe disease, often **as the fever falls**.
**Same-day assessment**: malaria test, FBC (platelets, haematocrit), NS1 / PCR or serology; **paracetamol and fluids only**.
**Severe dengue** (plasma leakage, bleeding, organ impairment); **NSAIDs or aspirin** raise bleeding risk.

cause.lead: A mosquito-borne flavivirus; worse the second time.
points: Most common travel-associated arbovirus in the UK (record **904** imported cases in 2024); mostly South / South-East Asia, also Latin America and the Caribbean.
*Aedes aegypti / albopictus*: **day-biting**, urban, breed in small clean standing water.
**Second infection with a different serotype** → antibody-dependent enhancement → more severe disease.
WHO 2009: without warning signs → with warning signs → severe.

visuals.caption: Dengue’s danger window: plasma leakage typically starts around days 3–7, just as the fever settles, so falling temperature isn’t reassurance on its own.
visuals.alt: Fever curve falling with a highlighted window and a leaking vessel

points: **Febrile** (days 1–3/7): abrupt high fever, **retro-orbital headache**, myalgia, arthralgia, back pain (‘break-bone’), vomiting; positive tourniquet test.
Rash in ~half (often missed on darker skin): early **flushing**; days 3–6 **morbilliform** exanthem from hands / feet; convalescent **‘white islands in a sea of red’**.

visuals.caption: Convalescent dengue rash: confluent redness with small round islands of spared pale skin, ‘white islands in a sea of red’.
visuals.alt: Lower leg with confluent red rash and white islands

points: Febrile returnee from a malarious area: **same-day films / RDT**.
FBC: **leucopenia, thrombocytopenia, rising haematocrit**; LFT, U&E, CRP.
Days 1–5/7: **RT-PCR / NS1**; after ~day 5: **IgM** (UKHSA RIPL); flavivirus cross-reactivity.

cards.name: Zika
cards.clue: Milder fever, itchy rash, conjunctivitis; pregnancy implications.

cards.name: Acute HIV seroconversion
cards.clue: Morbilliform rash, pharyngitis, nodes, oral ulcers.

manage.lead: No antiviral; supportive care and watchful timing.

points: Any fever in a returning traveller → same-day GP / urgent care / A&E (HTD walk-in if unwell): **not a pharmacy-only problem**.
**Paracetamol only** (standard doses; caution with liver involvement).
Oral fluids / ORS, rest, monitor urine output.
Outpatient only if senior-assessed without warning signs: **daily review / FBC** through days 3–7.

Bite avoidance **by day**: DEET 50% (adults, children > 2 months, pregnancy), sunscreen first then repellent; long sleeves, permethrin clothing; screens / AC; nets for daytime naps; remove standing water.
**Qdenga** (live, 2 doses 3 months apart): only ≥ 4 years **with previous dengue** travelling to risk areas (Green Book 15a).

limits.t: Avoid; don’t sell OTC to a febrile returnee. Avoid IM injections.

items.t: **Warning signs**: abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, mucosal bleeding, lethargy / restlessness, fluid accumulation, rising haematocrit with falling platelets.
Fever after the tropics: **exclude malaria the same day**.

pearls.t: Falling fever is the **danger window**, not the all-clear.
Febrile traveller asking for ibuprofen: **paracetamol only**.
*Aedes* bite by day: dusk-to-dawn advice isn’t enough.

quiz.a: ‘White islands in a sea of red’.

quiz.q: First test in a febrile returnee from a malarious area?
